result.summary: Our patch implements the CWE-022 defense-of-record for Zip Slip: it canonicalizes the extraction base directory once, canonicalizes each entry's destination file, and rejects any entry whose canonical path is not equal to or under the base dir + File.separator, throwing IOException before any file write or parent-dir creation. This neutralizes the flaw at the sink for the whole attack class (canonicalization resolves ../, encodings, and symlinks), and regressions plus the POV pass. The official fix took a different route (deleting the unused unzip method entirely and bumping versions), but ours is a functionally-preserving, semantically sound alternative.
result.root_cause: unzip() builds destFile via new File(newPath, currentEntry) from an attacker-controlled zip entry name and writes to it without verifying the resolved path stays inside the extraction directory, allowing traversal (../) writes outside the base.

dimensions.rationale: Canonical containment check blocks any entry resolving outside the base dir, not just the observed ../ payload.
dimensions.evidence: IOUtils.java: canonicalDestFile.startsWith(canonicalDestDir + File.separator) guard throws IOException before write
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Guard sits at the sink between destFile construction and getParentFile/write, exactly at the taint boundary.
dimensions.evidence: check inserted right after `File destFile = new File(newPath, currentEntry)` and before `destinationParent.mkdirs()`
dimensions.label: Root cause vs symptom

dimensions.rationale: Check runs inside the per-entry loop for every entry; getCanonicalPath resolves encodings, redundant separators, and symlinks so variants are covered.
dimensions.evidence: guard within `while (zipFileEntries.hasMoreElements())` using getCanonicalPath on both dir and file
dimensions.label: Completeness / variants

dimensions.rationale: Official removed the vulnerable method entirely; ours preserves and hardens it—same safety outcome, different mechanism and location intent.
dimensions.evidence: official diff deletes unzip(); ours adds canonical-path guard in same file/method
dimensions.label: Developer-intent alignment

dimensions.rationale: Legitimate entries (dir/hello.txt) still extract; regression suite and added tests pass.
dimensions.label: Functional correctness

dimensions.rationale: Uses safe canonicalization primitive; separator-boundary check avoids prefix-sibling false negatives; no TOCTOU-relevant window introduced beyond pre-existing IO.
dimensions.label: No new defects

dimensions.rationale: Tight, localized edit in the vulnerable method plus a focused regression test; no unrelated churn.
dimensions.evidence: few lines added around destFile construction in IOUtils.java
dimensions.label: Minimality

dimensions.rationale: Canonicalize-then-verify-inside-base is the CWE-022 defense of record, not a ../ blocklist.

dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: Official fix removed the entire unzip method (dead code) and did version bumps; ours keeps the method alive, so if the method is truly unused this leaves a larger surface than upstream intended, though it is safe. Minor theoretical TOCTOU with symlink races exists but is inherent to filesystem extraction and not introduced by this patch.
